messages.content: Determine the winner in a Poker game with John having a Hand of 8♥, 10♥, J♥, Q♥, K♥ and Mike having 9♠, J♠, 10♠, Q♠, K♠.

function.name: card_games_poker_determine_winner
function.description: Determines the winner in a game of Poker based on the cards in each players' hands. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

hand1.description: The list of cards (as strings) in first player's hand. E.g ['10♠', 'J♠']

hand2.description: The list of cards (as strings) in second player's hand. E.g ['9♥', '10♥']

message.content:
**Winner:** Mike

**Explanation:**  
Both hands are flushes (all cards of the same suit).  
- John’s flush: 8♥ – 10♥ – J♥ – Q♥ – K♥  
- Mike’s flush: 9♠ – 10♠ – J♠ – Q♠ – K♠  

When comparing flushes, we look at the highest card first. Both have a King (K).  
Next we compare the next highest cards: both have a Jack (J), then a Queen (Q), then a Ten (10).  
The deciding card is the fifth card: John has an 8, while Mike has a 9. Since 9 > 8, Mike’s flush is higher.

Therefore, **Mike wins the hand.**
message.reasoning: We need to determine winner. John has 8♥,10♥,J♥,Q♥,K♥. That's a straight flush from 8 to K? Actually 8-10-J-Q-K is a straight flush (8-9-10-J-Q-K would be 6 cards but we have 5). Wait we have 8,10,J,Q,K. Missing 9. So it's not a straight flush. It's a flush (all hearts) but not straight. Highest card K. Mike has 9♠,J♠,10♠,Q♠,K♠. That's also a flush (spades). Highest card K. But Mike has 9,10,J,Q,K. That's also a straight flush? No missing 8. So both are flushes. Compare high cards: both K. Next compare next highest: J vs J equal. Next Q vs Q equal. Next 10 vs 10 equal. Next 8 vs 9? John's 8, Mike's 9. So Mike's 9 is higher. So Mike wins. So answer: Mike wins.
